After the more "modern" experience of [b]Steel Strider[/b], Astro Port goes back to its roots here: just a shot button you can put a weight on, a bomb button, and that's it. While it gets frantic on harder difficulties, the game is not a bullet hell, and reminds me a lot of Toaplan games and especially [b]Raiden[/b], with those point bonuses revealed when some ground structures are destroyed, and one weapon being a lock-on laser, if not looking as great as the laser whip of [b]Raiden II[/b]. There is even a [i]tate[/i] mode if you can rotate the screen 90 degrees (I mean, I bought a monitor that can do that also to play games that support such a mode).

The game is awkwardly inserted into the Astro Saga timeline as something happening to a division of the Terran Defense Force (an army seen in other AP games), in some faraway place, a few years before [b]Gigantic Army[/b]. Totally unnecessary.

The power-up system is simple yet mildly original, as the pickup icons have arrows indicating on which side of the ship the weapon drone will be installed. I found the three weapons to be very balanced in their strengths and weaknesses, making a mix-and-match more convenient than just having both drones of the same type.

If you played any other AP game except [b]Vulkaiser[/b] and [b]Meglilo[/b], you know what to expect in terms of graphics, for the best: artist SAK is an accomplished mecha designer at this point, any enemy larger than a tank or turret sports great detail, and seeing the giant wrecks of some bosses is satisfactory. It could really pass for an arcade game of the 1990s.

While it's a vertical shooter, it scrolls also horizontally, with a generous portion of the playfield not visible at any time. It has implications even on the gameplay, as offscreen enemies wont' shoot, so occasionally taking "refuge" on a far side is a viable strategy to reduce pressure from the enemies.

The most annoying element, noted by some other reviews, is the abundance of "sniper" enemies which constantly trail the player and shoot oblong purple bullets that, while clear to see over the backgrounds, are very fast and may be shot even quite close. Of course being constantly on the move is the way but even so, sometimes the window of opportunity to avoid such bullets is too short. Tanks and turrets, usually the low level fodder you save for last while dealing with bigger units, are the dangers to clear out first and faster here. It was not a surprise to me that the first phase of the final boss has it also releasing tanks at regular intervals.

[b]WOLFLAME[/b] is a short game but, with 10 stages each with a boss (although the Level 7 boss is quite unimpressive compared to Level 6's), it's also a bit longer than average for the genre and, in any case, it's not a game played on the prospect that it takes hours to reach the end but to make a better run eacht time - or relax shooting down things on Easy! For such low price, it's a steal.

So many things can show up and immediately kill you like pop up turrets, or aircraft showing up at the edge of the screen. Bombs are for defense. Always stay mobile. 

STORY TIME! (or extended review or something)
This is the first game I've played in the "upgrade ship midgame" genre. I did beat the game on normal difficulty with minimal gear level and that was a massive pain in the butt. I died like 150 times through that. The repetitiveness of dying so often to enemy's quick attacks was tiring. This game is mathematically designed to kill you. 
-The upgrade system takes your attention away from the enemies too. 
-The game's story is exclusively told on the Steam store page, and on Steam trading cards. I prefer to make up my own story for this game. 
After I learned to reload, I now love the game. Also, screenshots on the store page are inaccurate. In the actual game there's some metal backround filling the sides of the screen up to 4:3 ratio. And high score doesn't save if you do New Game. Taught me the lesson that survival is better than score, so I ignore the shiny medals. 
-"The Long Haul" Steam achievement guide: I achieved it by doing NEW GAME, on EASY. If I died, I would do RESTART. Did it in one sitting too. 
-Dangerous tip: The closer you are to the enemy, the higher your damage output, but you're closer to the enemy, so...
-[b]Terrible tip[/b] I've heard: "Many bullets are just for show". No, any bullet or aircraft on the screen is an immediate threat. You must've not noticed because you pretend to play the game. (Dislikers really haven't tried.)

The other shmups I like are The Guardian Legend, Caladrius Blaze, Angel at Dusk, Natsuki Chronicles, and R-Type III. Cygni isn't as bad as people said, and Zero Ranger is also pretty good.

I first tried [b]Satazius[/b] and [b]Zangeki Warp[/b] and within the first couple of levels in those games I ran into some trial & error or gotcha! style traps.  

I was pleasantly surprised to see that [b]Wolflame[/b], while less colourful and showy than say, [b]Satazius[/b] at least wasn't doing this to me.  I was having quite a bit of fun and it was bringing games like [b]Raiden[/b] and [b]Tyrian[/b] to mind.  I actually thought this was going to be a positive rec when I was more than halfway through the game.

At some point though, I encountered a bullet pattern that slowly closed around me, leaving me with no way out.  I had a bit more patience for the [i]Gotcha![/i] this time, as I was a number of levels deep and more invested in the experience by the time this happened.  I pushed on, and then in a later level it happened again.  This time I was on the left side of the screen, and enemies came in from that direction right on top of me, instantly killing me before I could react.  The issue is there is no warning or telegraph.

I was still hanging in there with [b]Wolflame[/b], until stage 7 or 8, when the game started throwing a lot more tanks at me.  Tanks suck.  These enemies fire projectiles VERY fast.  They're like snipers that are targetting you for a while and then let off a fast shot, so fast that you can barely dodge out of the way.  There had been a few of these earlier in the game, but now I was having to deal with hordes of them.  You're kind of forced to take them out or hide out of range of them.  But it feels like a real crap shoot trying to deal with them and not in a way I find fun.  

Now just because I hate the tanks (and some of the other negative rec players hate the tanks) doesn't mean you won't enjoy trying to deal with them, but I digress.

The music is.. harmless.  Lively vibes in the background but nothing memorable or exciting going on with it.

I do feel that with a little more polish, these games could be more accessible and less frustrating than they are currently.

Wolflame é um jogo estranho, definitivamente um jogo estranho.

Ele é simples, bem barato, extremamente apegado ao básico em tudo e fica nisso. Poderia ser uma experiência divertida mas existe um enorme desbalanceamento dentro do jogo. O jogo tem 4 dificuldades, e o jogo obviamente te orienta a jogar no Normal, mas o Normal é insano de difícil e o Easy é fácil demais (exceto as duas fases finais).

Sabendo disso, nem dá vontade de testar o Hard ou Insane, porque não existe um bom balanço do jogo em aprender e decorar os padrões pra depois voltar em dificuldades maiores. Além disso, a música é um plano de fundo, soa como se fosse totalmente inexistente (o que é MUITO estranho porque shmups geralmente tem trilhas sonoras boas, embora nem todas memoráveis), a bomba é sem graça e não é muito gratificante dar power-up na nave, até porque ela morre muito rápido.

Isso devido ao problema da sua nave ser MUITO LENTA num jogo que não é bullet hell, mas os inimigos comuns como tanques e naves atiram em você numa velocidade que beira o sônico em certos momentos. Mesmo no Easy vai ter momentos que vai morrer no susto porque não dá pra reagir as balas, você precisa estar se movimentando ANTES de algo vir até você, mesmo que no caminho você se choque com outras balas ou inimigos, lasers, e afins.

Wolflame é um jogo bonito, apesar de genéricos os gráficos são muito bons apesar de simples, e só. Pois todo o resto é chato demais se for no Easy ou frustrante demais se for no Normal, o que com certeza me faz nem ter vontade de jogar nas demais dificuldades. Um shmup sem música marcante, desafio sem balanço e nenhum modo extra, sem dúvida é um jogo lançado. 

Nao é ruim. Mas é frustrante e sem muito conteúdo. Na dúvida, jogue no fácil e o Normal deixe pra depois. Pelo menos o 100% dele é relativamente tranquilo em vista dos demais jogos do gênero na Steam.

Ele beira os 10 reais em promoções, mas com isso você pode comprar Super Galaxy Squadron, Caladrius Blaze, Ikaruga, Touhou Makaka, Super XYX, entre outros jogos que são tão simples como esse (e melhores) ou que possuem mais conteúdo que justifique. A menos que queira ter e deixar na coleção e se desafiar, aí pode ser que seja uma boa dose de entretenimento.

Man, I really wanted to like Wolflame. I really did. But I guess some stuff are unachievable.

The game starts strong, VERY STRONG if I may say. Destroying enemy troops, combining the special pickups into weapons of mass destruction... the game just feels so fun. But the more you progress into the game, the more you can see its flaws.
I do not want to waste my or your time explaining the obvious good points of the game as it is not wildly different compared to your usual shmup game, so I'll just skip to the critiques and their explanations.

- Setting the pause keybind to Enter/Return completely breaks this function, as the game registers the button two times and will immediately resume the game. So don't be me and don't do that.

- As many others have mentioned, some of the enemies fire a singular, very fast bullet type that is very hard to dodge if you are in a pinch or if you are not already moving around when they fire it. And as the game gets a habit of spamming these enemies during later levels, a lot of your deaths will mostly come from them. Some might say the ship is too slow for this bullet type, but I'd like to argue that the rest of the game has not been built around it instead, as when you are not encountering the aforementioned bullet type the game plays very well and very fair. However the moment you see the enemies that shoot it, you'll be more likely to scroll to and stay on a safe side of the screen rather than risk getting shot.

- Usefulness of the life system is debatable. Every enemy projectile is a one hit kill and there are no shields either. However, upon taking a hit, you will not be able to continue on the spot and will instead be forced to continue from a past checkpoint. Not unusual for a shmup game, but there are two big issues with this system:
1. You will lose every special weapon you have and unless the game throws one at you, you will be utterly outgunned.
2. You are able to reclaim your lost weapons after killing some enemies, but if you die again before getting them, they are gone for good and you will be forced to use the weak default shot.
These issues can effectively leave you in a very vulnerable state. You cannot properly attack to save your life and can die again in one hit anyway.

- Boss fights are very lackluster. Sometimes the bosses don't actually look threatening design-wise (some of them look like normal enemies that can appear in middle of a level), and sometimes the battles are really not that exciting. It doesn't help that the game does not spice things up properly using sights and sound. You do hear a low volume alert sound, but cannot expect anything like flashing WARNING logos, high energy boss music or similar. Bosses are by far the easiest and the most boring part of the game.

- The bomb is ineffective in protecting you from some enemy attacks. For example, there's a carrier missile in the final level that releases homing swarm missiles after getting destroyed. If the carrier missile is close to you and you use a bomb, you will still die. I assume this is because the swarm missiles have a very brief invincibility period so their appearance animation can be finished.


So overall, I personally do not recommend playing this game. It's not Satazius levels of being disappointing, but does leave you in a conflicted state as you really want to like the game, but various design choices of the game makes you unable to.

Wolfflame is a vertical scrolling shooter that reminds me of  Truxton. In Wolflame, you start with the basic guns and limited area damaging, enemy bullet soaking bombs.  During the level you gain upgrades that place a satellite on your left and/or right side with one of three shots. Either a green powerful beam, blue lock-on front beam(s) and homing missiles.  With each power up cycling through each weapon type as the bounce around the field of play over time.  And (at least for the easier settings so for) in the event your ship is destroyed, after a bit you'll get a chance to recover all your power ups with a red cross.

The enemies are plentiful, but they tend not to shoot often on the easier settings. The few bullets that are shot are usually at your ship's location and travel quickly there.  Not to say there aren't set bullet pattern attacks too.  Just that those attacks are usually reserved for the larger enemies and boss battles.  Wolframe seems to be more about keeping your ship on the move and dispatching enemies as quick as possible.  And fully upgraded satellites  give you plenty of firepower to make that happen.

The easy setting is pretty easy.  I'm a casual shmup fan, and I made it to level 5 (of 9 or 10) on my first playthrough not using bombs at all.  Again, the game being less about dodging and more about not stilling still.  And as more of casual shmup fan, I really like a game that I can sit down and play a good 20 minutes on 1CC without a ton of practice.  That might not beat the game, but it also feels like a good amount of progress on a single credit.

O sistema de armas é interessante, me lembrou um pouco Radiant Silver Gun, fora a bomba, são três armas diferentes (cada lado da nave pode ser armado com uma das três variações) em 5 níveis de intensidade. Recomendo o laser azul que trava automaticamente nos inimigos mais próximos. Se por um lado Wolflame não tem nada inovador, por outro é um Shmup muito competente e honesto na proposta de oferecer uma experiência "anos 90", ainda mais considerando o preço reduzido, principalmente durante as promoções Steam.

I rate the game WOLFLAME 4/5. Good.

This is a fun little vertically scrolling schmup arcade style action game in the style of the early Raiden games. WOLFLAME differs from the early Raiden games though by giving you an infinite number of 'continues' which has the effect of making the game much easier and far less frustrating.

+Adequate, old-style late 1980's/early 1990's arcade game graphics with an extremely nice, nostalgic quality to them which is heavily reminiscent of the first few Raiden games (and other, similar styled arcade games from the early 1990s).
+Good, simple and responsive controls.
+Simple, easy-to-use menus.
+Good, though still fairly standard-feeling weapon upgrades.
+As you progress, the game's areas scale up in difficulty slowly but surely even on the easiest difficulty. This game features several difficulty levels for good replay value.
+Great game for the fairly low price of 6 dollars (and that's not even when this game is on a special sale).

+/-Enemies and levels are fairly standard for this type of game.
+/-Mediocre though not annoying sound effects and music. Mostly just generic sounding for this type of game.

-This game never gives you a great sense of speed. Indeed, the levels/areas scroll past fairly slowly.
-Certain bosses seemed underwhelming and a little repetitive (there are at least 2 levels which use some sort of tank or tanks as the main boss but that's still ok though because big tanks are cool, especially in this kind of game).
-There is only a single type of fighter craft which you can control.
-Perhaps the absolute worst thing that can be said concerning this game is that it may very well be a severe rip-off of the early Raiden games. That said, WOLFLAME is fairly well-done nonetheless and provides a great, nostalgic, classic arcade feel. If you collect vertically scrolling Schmup games (like I do), you should definitely buy this one too, at least when it goes on a special sale.

[h1]Verdict: Recommended.[/h1]

I'm a complete sucker for Astro Port's stuff, but I'm particularly happy with Wolflame. I loved Satazius, their horizontally-scrolling homage to shoot-em-ups like Gradius, and Wolflame is the same level of homage to vertically-scrolling titles like Raiden. 

Your ship can acquire two satellites, each of which shoots one of three different weapons and can be upgraded five times. When a power-up appears, it changes color as it moves around the screen, allowing you to switch each satellite's weapon type on the fly by grabbing it when it is the desired color. Having a fully upgraded set of satellites makes you feel powerful, but not invulnerable, especially at higher difficulty levels. My favorite aspect of the upgrade system is being able to recover your previous abilities after you die, if you are lucky enough to spawn the proper power-up icon and collect it with your new ship.

The graphics nail the intended retro aesthetic, and cover the usual variety of environments (land, sea, outer space). The game ran smoothly at 60 FPS on everything I tried, including a laptop with Intel 5000 integrated graphics. There are basic configuration options for resolution, controls, and difficulty. If you're looking for something to scratch a retro arcade shooter itch, give this a try!

You lose everything on death, which is a little unfair in later levels. But well, the developer is trying to make a Raiden clone so that's fine if you like the origin.

The game has 10 levels, considering it's a shoot em up, that's a lot. And there is a Save/Load function, you can save the game anywhere and load to start from that level. This is handy when you find yourself hard to concentrate after a few levels, or when you made some really silly mistakes.

And this game has 4 difficulties, Easy is really easy(I managed to 1cc in my first try, with a little bit luck), you can also get almost all achievements by just playing easy(Only 1 exception, you have to complete normal, with infinite continues). That's very friendly to beginners, which is something really lacking in the shoot em up genre.

Another excellent shoot 'em up from Astro Port. This one is heavily remiscent of early 90's Toaplan classics such as Fire Shark, Truxton and Twin Cobra - i.e. not a bullet hell shooter. Tight gameplay, good graphics, well recommended!

As [i]Satazius is to Gradius[/i], and [i]Gigantic Army[/i] is to [i]Assault Suit Valken[/i], then [i]Wolflame[/i] is very much in the spirit of Toaplan. The deal with Toaplan shootemups is that they excel at the fundamentals. When you play one of these classic games, you're not going to be dazzled by fountains of pretty bullets and thousands of shiny gold medals. Every moment of these games is a life or death struggle. The one tank that you miss just might be the one that takes you down. ASTRO PORT delivers yet another thriller that is sure to please any shmup fan.

Like most other shmups, [i]Wolflame[/i] has no story to speak of. The goal is to destroy everything, collect a few medals, and try not to get shot down too often. The scoring system is pretty basic. All of the medals you collect in a stage are cashed in at the end for a lot of points, provided you don't die and lose them. Actually, you might as well try not to die at all, because spare lives are worth a ton as well. Unlike most shooters, there's no huge penalty for using bullet-clearing bombs. Even if you manage to collect a full stock, any extras are worth a measly 100 points each.

There are two kinds of bullets in this game, the kind that distract you, and the kind that kill you. The killer bullets are easy to spot. They're purple, thin, and fast. Most of the enemies that fire purple bullets are tanks, turrets, and so on. It's actually pretty sensible, since smaller ships don't have the power to maintain control, while firing such a powerful weapon. Typically, the killer bullets are fired when the enemy has you in their sights, so if you're not constantly moving, then you're probably going to die. As soon as a tank appears on-screen, either destroy it or get out of the way, because they're extremely deadly.

That's not to say there aren't any of the typical bullet-spreads we associate with STGs, but they're only a part of the threat. These slow yet plentiful bullets are there to catch your eye, force you into bad situations, and basically "herd" you into just the right spot. What happens next? If you guessed that a tank would appear practically out of nowhere and snipe you, then congrats! Your prize is a trip back to the last checkpoint.

Yes, Wolflame is a checkpoint-based shooter. That means you don't instantly respawn when you die. Thankfully, there's usually a nearby power-up that restores all of your lost weapons. The checkpoints are also a lot more reasonable than some of the earliest shmups. Still, getting kicked backwards upon death can be very punishing. Having to re-do bosses as well as brutal segments can chew through your spare lives pretty quickly.

One more thing: Like a number of vertical shooters, the screen shifts slightly to the left or right depending on your position. This can be useful, because enemies don't fire when they're off-screen. However, you also want to make a mental note of any enemies that are off-screen, just so you don't move over and suddenly get point-blank blasted by a killer bullet. 

It's interesting that [i]Twin Cobra[/i] is mentioned in the store-description for this game. [i]Twin Cobra[/i] is the game that got me to fear tanks again. After several years of danmaku bullet-hells, where avoiding billions of bullets almost becomes effortless, I was re-introduced to the dreaded tank. Tanks in [i]Twin Cobra[/i] only fire one bullet, but one bullet is enough in a shmup. [i]Wolflame[/i] understands that same philosophy, and its legions of meticulously placed tanks and turrets are sure to confound and enrage a new generation of gamers.
